hook.text: Stephin Merritt first pictured it as a stage show with four drag queens, then settled on sixty-nine songs instead of a hundred.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: April 1999 at Polar West, Mother West, Polar Mother and Sonics

sentences.text: Stephin Merritt was in a Manhattan gay piano bar, hearing a pianist's takes on Stephen Sondheim songs, when he resolved to move into theatre music.
He believed he had a knack for it.
He had also read about Charles Ives's 114 Songs that day, and it inspired him.
Other influences included Fleetwood Mac, Billie Holiday and Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark.
Much of the writing was done in Dick's Bar, a New York bar, and Stephin Merritt said he spent eight hours a day there.
He is credited on many instruments, from ukulele and autoharp to musical saw and thunder sheet.
Merritt also engineered the record, with help from Jon Berman, Chris Ewen, Claudia Gonson, Eric Masunaga and Charles Newman.
Other singers, among them Dudley Klute, LD Beghtol and Shirley Simms, sing on several songs.
The songs move between country, synth-pop and free jazz, with sorrowful ballads too.
Every song still deals with love, though often with irony or a quirky slant.
The band played all 69 songs in order seven times, five in the US and two in London.
When played live, some of the big orchestrations were arranged more simply because of limited performers or equipment.
Circus released it in Europe and Australia in May 2000, and Domino reissued it in the UK.
Other artists have covered several songs, among them Peter Gabriel with 'The Book of Love' and Superchunk with 'I Don't Want to Get Over You' in 2025.

listen_for.track: The Luckiest Guy on the Lower East Side
listen_for.text: Dudley Klute sings lead on it, and Ida Pearle plays violin.

listen_for.track: Time Enough for Rocking When We're Old
listen_for.text: John Woo plays banjo, lead guitar, mandolin and bass on it.
Shirley Simms duets with Merritt on it.
Daniel Handler plays accordion and keyboards on it.
Chris Ewen plays theremin on it.
